# heatwaveR

**heatwaveR** provides fast, research-grade tools to detect, classify,
and visualise heatwaves and cold-spells in daily or hourly temperature
data.

Use it to build climatologies, identify events, summarise metrics, make
publication-ready figures.

**heatwaveR** is the modern, faster successor to
[**RmarineHeatWaves**](https://github.com/ajsmit/RmarineHeatWaves),
which in turn was the original R translation of
[marineHeatWvaes](https://github.com/ecjoliver/marineHeatWaves). This
package implements the Hobday et al. conventions that are used by many
marine heatwave researchers around the world.

[![CRAN version
badge](https://www.r-pkg.org/badges/version/heatwaveR)](https://cran.r-project.org/package=heatwaveR)
[![R CMD check
badge](https://github.com/robwschlegel/heatwaveR/workflows/R-CMD-check/badge.svg)](https://github.com/robwschlegel/heatwaveR/actions)
[![Codecov
badge](https://codecov.io/gh/robwschlegel/heatwaveR/branch/master/graph/badge.svg)](https://app.codecov.io/gh/robwschlegel/heatwaveR?branch=master)
[![JOSS
badge](https://joss.theoj.org/papers/10.21105/joss.00821/status.svg)](https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.00821)

## Install

Install the CRAN release:

``` r
install.packages("heatwaveR")
```

Install the development version:

``` r
devtools::install_github("robwschlegel/heatwaveR")
```

## Start here

### Detect events

Build seasonal climatologies and identify heatwaves or cold-spells with
[`ts2clm()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/ts2clm.md)
and
[`detect_event()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/detect_event.md).

[Basic detection and
visualisation](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/detection_and_visualisation.html)

### Classify severity

Add Hobday et al. event categories, summarise metrics, and compare
events across years or locations.

[Event category
workflow](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/event_categories.html)

### Scale to gridded data

Prepare OISST or other gridded inputs, then move into larger workflows
with **heatwave3**.

[Gridded event
detection](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/gridded_event_detection.html)

## Core functions

| Function | Role |
|----|----|
| [`ts2clm()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/ts2clm.md) / [`ts2clm3()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/ts2clm3.md) | Construct seasonal climatologies and thresholds from a time series. |
| [`detect_event()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/detect_event.md) / [`detect_event3()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/detect_event3.md) | Detect heatwaves or cold-spells and return full event metrics. |
| [`category()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/category.md) | Apply Hobday et al. (2018) event categories. |
| [`exceedance()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/exceedance.md) | Detect consecutive exceedances relative to a static threshold. |
| [`block_average()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/block_average.md) | Summarise event metrics at annual or block scale. |
| [`event_line()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/event_line.md), [`lolli_plot()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/lolli_plot.md), [`geom_flame()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/geom_flame.md), [`geom_lolli()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/geom_lolli.md) | Create publication-ready visualisations of detected events. |

The package also ships example SST records for historical events in the
Mediterranean, Northwest Atlantic, and Western Australia.

## Where to go next

- Browse the [reference
  index](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/index.html)
  for function-level details.
- Work through the [articles
  index](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/index.html)
  for practical workflows.
- Explore the [interactive
  demo](https://robert-schlegel.shinyapps.io/demoMHW/) for a quick
  hands-on overview.
- See the [Marine Heatwave
  Tracker](https://www.marineheatwaves.org/tracker.html) for a live
  global application.
- Check the [citations
  page](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/CITATIONS.html) for
  published uses of the package.

## Citation

If you use **`heatwaveR`** in research or reporting, please cite:

Schlegel, R. W., & Smit, A. J. (2018). *heatwaveR: A central algorithm
for the detection of heatwaves and cold-spells*. Journal of Open Source
Software, 3(27), 821. <https://doi.org/10.21105/joss.00821>

In R:

``` r
citation("heatwaveR")
```

# Package index

## Detect and Classify

Core tools for building climatologies and identifying events.

- [`ts2clm()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/ts2clm.md)
  : Make a climatology from a daily time series.
- [`ts2clm3()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/ts2clm3.md)
  : Make a climatology from a daily time series.
- [`detect_event()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/detect_event.md)
  : Detect heatwaves and cold-spells.
- [`detect_event3()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/detect_event3.md)
  : Detect heatwaves and cold-spells.
- [`exceedance()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/exceedance.md)
  : Detect consecutive days in exceedance above or below of a given
  threshold.
- [`category()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/category.md)
  : Calculate the categories of events.

## Summarise and Visualise

Event summaries and publication-ready plotting helpers.

- [`block_average()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/block_average.md)
  : Calculate yearly means for event metrics.
- [`event_line()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/event_line.md)
  : Create a line plot of heatwaves or cold-spells.
- [`lolli_plot()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/lolli_plot.md)
  : Create a timeline of selected event metrics as 'lollipops'.
- [`geom_flame()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/geom_flame.md)
  : Create 'flame' polygons.
- [`geom_lolli()`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/geom_lolli.md)
  : Visualise a timeline of several event metrics as 'lollipops'.

## Example Data

Observed temperature records used throughout the documentation.

- [`Algiers`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/Algiers.md)
  : Daily maximum (tX) and minimum (tN) air temperatures for Algiers,
  Algeria.
- [`sst_Med`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/sst_Med.md)
  : NOAA Optimally Interpolated (OI) v2.1 daily 1/4 degree SST for the
  Mediterranean region.
- [`sst_NW_Atl`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/sst_NW_Atl.md)
  : NOAA Optimally Interpolated (OI) v2.1 daily 1/4 degree SST for the
  NW Atlantic region.
- [`sst_WA`](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/reference/sst_WA.md)
  : NOAA Optimally Interpolated (OI) v2.1 daily 1/4 degree SST for the
  Western Australian region.

# Articles

### Get Started

Core workflows for day-to-day package use.

- [Basic Detection and Visualisation of
  Events](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/detection_and_visualisation.md):

  This vignette demonstrates the basic use of the heatwaveR package for
  the detection and visualisation of events.

- [Calculating and Visualising Event
  Categories](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/event_categories.md):

  This vignette deomonstrates how to calculate and visualise the
  categories for events.

- [Calculating and Visualising
  Exceedances](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/exceedance.md):

  This vignette demonstrates the use of the exceedence function.

### Advanced Workflows

Alternative thresholds, trend analysis, gridded data, and export
pipelines.

- [Alternative
  Thresholds](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/complex_clims.md):

  This vignette walks the user through multiple different options for
  creating and applying thresholds outside of the default settings.

- [Trend and Breakpoint analyses in MHW
  metrics](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/MHW_metric_trends.md):

  This vignette demonstrates the utility and limitation of running a
  trend and break point analyses in MHW metrics.

- [Downloading and Preparing NOAA OISST
  Data](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/OISST_preparation.md):

  This vignette demonstrates how to download NOAA OISST data and prepare
  them for the detection of marine heatwaves.

- [Detecting Events in Gridded
  Data](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/gridded_event_detection.md):

  This vignette demonstrates how to detect marine heatwaves (MHWs) in
  dataframes of gridded data in which each pixel is a separate time
  series.

- [Download, Prepare, and Analyse NOAA OISST Data: Alternative
  Methods](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/Download_SST_v2.md):

  This vignette demonstrates an alternative method for downloading NOAA
  OISST data (using a python script) and preparing and detecting marine
  heatwaves.

- [Saving MHW Results to
  NetCDF](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/MHW_to_nc.md):

  This vignette demonstrates how to save marine heatwaves (MHWs)
  detected from gridded data as a NetCDF file.

### Package Internals

Development notes and internal workflow documentation.

- [heatwaveR internal
  workflow](https://robwschlegel.github.io/heatwaveR/articles/internal_workflow.md):

  This vignette outlines the internal workflow structure of the
  heatwaveR package.
